items.title: Live: Trump says US military will remain in Middle East until an agreement is reached — or shooting will start again
items.description: Donald Trump says if an agreement is not reached, the "shootin' starts bigger and better and stronger than anyone has ever seen before". Follow live.

items.title: Breaking: High Court refuses to hear Bruce Lehrmann's appeal
items.description: The High Court was Bruce Lehrmann's last legal avenue to challenge a Federal Court ruling that found, on the balance of probabilities, he did rape Brittany Higgins.

items.title: 'Running on the street screaming': Beirut faces war's most intense attacks
items.description: As a shaky ceasefire struggles to get under way, deadly Israeli strikes on Lebanon risk worsening the Middle East conflict.

items.title: Is Hormuz open or closed? Shiptracking data reveals true picture
items.description: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has remained at an effective standstill in the 24 hours since Iran conditionally lifted its blockade on the critical shipping lane, amid a fragile ceasefire with the US and Israel.

items.title: Live: Oil rallies as doubts about US-Iran ceasefire grow
items.description: Oil prices are higher following growing concerns the US and Iran's two-week ceasefire may now on the brink of collapse. Follow live.

items.title: Top neuroscientist slams AFL move to back new headgear
items.description: The AFL has backed a new helmet that aims to reduce the risk of concussion, but a top neuroscientist is calling it "bad scientific practice".

items.title: Singapore's PM knows Australia is vulnerable but Albanese has leverage
items.description: Anthony Albanese is flying to Singapore as part of a hastily arranged regional mission to shore up crucial fuel supplies, amid warnings the global energy crisis could "sharply turn for the worse".

items.title: China's 26 phone calls that brought on a US-Iran ceasefire
items.description: China's Foreign Minister Wang Yi says he held 26 phone calls with his counterparts in Iran, Israel, Russia and Gulf countries before the ceasefire was reached.

items.title: Trump criticises NATO over Iran in meeting with alliance's boss
items.description: US President Donald Trump vents his frustration with NATO during a private meeting with its secretary-general as relations in the military alliance reach a crisis point over the Iran war.

items.title: Uni in financial crisis spent nearly $1.5m on leadership coach, documents show
items.description: Documents released to Four Corners show the University of Technology Sydney spent hundreds of thousands of dollars a year on a leadership coach before planning to slash jobs and courses to save money.

items.title: People living in vehicles forced to choose between fuel and food
items.description: The high cost of fuel is making it even more difficult for people living in their cars to afford food, electricity and transport.

items.title: Hundreds more PSOs at Melbourne stations if Liberals win state election
items.description: The Victorian Opposition is promising to recruit hundreds more protective service officers if it wins government in November.

items.title: First glimpse of $600m Sydney Metro West rail designs
items.description: The NSW government says the transport hubs will connect commuters from western areas of Sydney to the CBD in "under 20 minutes".

items.title: Large fire damages roof of Olympic velodrome
items.description: Rio de Janeiro's Olympic velodrome has been damaged following a fire, which required about 80 firefighters and 20 fire trucks to bring under control.

items.title: Woman charged after man allegedly struck with hammer in Sydney hospital
items.description: A woman has been charged after allegedly attacking a man with a hammer at a Sydney hospital overnight.

items.title: $1m reward in 2003 cold-case death of Harmony Bryant
items.description: Police hope a $1 million reward will produce fresh information about the death of a 26-year-old Kyogle  woman, who was found suffering severe burns in bushland on the NSW Mid North Coast.

items.title: Comedian Grace Jarvis on most bizarre encounter working in sex shop
items.description: Grace Jarvis talks about everything from her experiences with autism, ADHD, queerness, and working in a sex shop in her stand-up. Her experiences with chronic illness? Not so much.

items.title: Four holes-in-one as 8yo steals show on Masters eve
items.description: The annual Par 3 Contest on the eve of the US Masters has produced four aces, but Tommy Fleetwood's eight-year-old son stole the show at Augusta National.

items.title: Tigers searching for third straight win to end eight-year streak
items.description: The last time Wests Tigers won three matches in a row, Ivan Cleary was still the club's coach and Benji Marshall had just begun his comeback as a player. Now, after eight years of waiting, they have the chance to end that streak.

items.title: 'Preferred profit … over the environment': Farm owner fined for clearing 112 hectares of bushland
items.description: The owner of a farm in South Australia's south-east is convicted and fined for clearing 112 hectares of bushland, but the penalty is much less than the $2.2 million he would have had to pay for a permit for the work.

items.title: Homicide investigation launched in Perth's north after 69yo man dies
items.description: A man dies in hospital after an altercation at a home in Padbury, and police say a 39-year-old man arrested at the scene is assisting investigators with their inquiries.

items.title: $10m horse will never race, but owner insists she is worth every cent
items.description: An owner says she has "no regrets" after announcing that the first filly from champion race mare Winx will never race.

items.title: Four charged for alleged offences 'connected' to murder of Adelaide father Chris Robertson
items.description: Four people have been arrested by police for alleged offences "connected" to the alleged murder of Adelaide father-of-two Chris Robertson last year.

items.title: Australian playwright wins $250k international award
items.description: S Shakthidharan, whose plays include The Wrong Gods, The Jungle and the Sea and Counting and Cracking, has won the prestigious Windham-Campbell Prize.

items.title: 'I've got my visa back': Child sex offender allowed to stay in Australia
items.description: Edward James Kilbey's permanent visa was automatically cancelled when he was jailed in 2024 for sexually abusing a nine-year-old girl, but a tribunal has upheld the 83-year-old's appeal in part due to his "ill health".
